note: Nucleus residency (architecture 4.2): two tiers. One entry per kernel object linked into the production image (the objects of linker/zephyr80.lk); tools/mapcheck.py fails the build when an object is missing or when a fixed-required object is compiled into the cold areas. Tiers: fixed-required = code that executes, or data that is touched, while the window shows another bank - it must link inside 2000h-5FFFh; cold = everything else that belongs to bank 7 (the syscall side, boot, the VFS core, process management and the driver loader). Every object is placed, and the cold data base follows the linked cold code.

tiers.fixed-required: Must be visible in the 2000h-5FFFh fixed core: the gates and transition code, the copy primitives, the IRQ executive, the ROMFS bootstrap reader, the processes' raw entry, common-resident boot/panic code and the stacks. mapcheck rejects a fixed-required object whose bytes link at or above 6000h.
tiers.cold: Belongs to bank 7's cold half (6000h-DFFFh), reached only while the window shows bank 7 (P = 0): the syscall dispatcher and bodies, boot and idle, process management, the VFS core, the resident-driver loader and the diagnostics.

objects.reason: common-resident latch and mode gates: the only mapping-changing code, always visible

zero-byte ABS label exporting __kernel_code_end, the exclusive end of the linked cold code; the object emits no linked bytes and carries the derived build/geometry/bank7_end.inc, so it stays out of cold_half (the residency-driven codegen flags cannot propagate down its dependency on the generated include)
the VFS root router (bind/unbind/resolve, ns_enum and the namespace operations): reached only through the syscall dispatcher or the driver loader, both with P = 0
the /dev DEVICE provider table: called from the router with P = 0
the /fs forwarding provider: called from the router with P = 0
the /system ROMFS FILE provider and its metadata reader, called from the router with P = 0
bind/call/unbind/ns_enum/chdir/getcwd bodies, reached from the syscall dispatcher with P = 0
diagnostic syscall bodies, reached only through the syscall dispatcher, which the gate runs with P = 0
extended-memory syscall bodies, the object table and the aperture token: reached only through the syscall dispatcher, which the gate runs with P = 0
diagnostic port primitives reached only from the diagnostic syscall bodies (P = 0)
common-resident early console and panic path: must survive any mapping
IRQ registry and dispatch: the executive runs while the window shows the owner's bank (driver-owned IRQs), so its code and data stay visible
linked end of the fixed _CODE area and the SDCC IY trampoline used by the IRQ path
common-resident IRQ stubs and gate; it carries the relocated ISR stack (5F00h-6000h) in its own ABS area
CTC quiesce source driver, called by the dispatcher while the owner's window is open
IM2 vector page in common memory: fetched with whatever mapping is active
kernel boot and idle path: every driver-facing call returns with the caller's latch restored, so it only ever runs with P = 0
string helpers called by the fixed ROMFS bootstrap reader while the window may show another bank
page-zero RST 30h material: must be present in every mode
common-resident panic path: must survive any mapping
IRQ platform bring-up (IM2 vector page, interrupt mode): common-resident
process lifecycle; the exit notification is a nucleus -> VFS upcall through a fixed shim, so the body is cold
exec/exit and the continuation stack; the executable-stream read is a nucleus -> VFS upcall through a fixed shim
common-resident raw application entry jump: no window-visible state
ROM-resident page-zero reset copier: runs before any mapping exists
common-resident ROM-read stub mirrored into every ROM page (mode 00)
the one ROMFS reader, kept in the nucleus as the bootstrap-reader primitive a bank-6 provider calls through the fixed core
SDCC runtime helpers called from fixed code and from IRQ handlers
common-resident boot entry and C runtime init: runs before the window exists
syscall dispatcher and its bodies: the syscall gate clears the page field before dispatching, so this object only ever runs with P = 0
the syscall transition gate is common-resident by contract (always visible); it saves the caller's whole latch, dispatches with P = 0 and restores exactly
common-resident application-bank copy gate (mode-10 crossings from common memory)
mode-11 window copy for auxiliary slots 3-6: runs with the window showing bank 7 - bank, where only the fixed core and common memory answer; fixed keeps the cost off the scarce common region

the upcall shim: cold code that calls a resident driver saves the latch, selects the window page, calls and restores; its code, its continuation and its request state must stay visible while the window shows another bank
VFS core: path normalization, cold code beside the syscall dispatcher and the driver loader
VFS core: the handle table and the per-process CWD pool, production cold code beside the syscall dispatcher and the driver loader
the path view a resident driver reads: the frame handed to a bank-6 dispatch names the path by address, so the workspace is touched while the window shows bank 6 (the buffer rule)

the IPC substrate (architecture 4.9): the endpoint table, call dispatch, the frame array, the descriptor table and the copy resolvers execute, and are touched, while the window shows bank 6, so they must link inside 2000h-5FFFh

fixed-core IPC primitives (kernel/ipc/ipc_asm.asm): the latch save/select/restore, the window LDIR and the driver-stack switch, plus the absolute declaration of the 512-byte driver stack at KOS_DRIVER_STACK_BASE

the common-resident aperture copy (kernel/ipc/ipc_common.asm): the path-B primitive runs with mode 10 and page 1 in force, where bank 7 is not mapped, so its code, its request block, its saved latch/SP and its interrupt-push stack must all be common; it shares the common ceiling with the mode-11 window copy

the resident-driver loader (kernel/driver/driver_loader.c, architecture 3.2 and 5.3): reads the boot manifest through the fixed ROMFS reader, places every driver image through the common application-bank copy gate, and runs the boot segments and hot inits. It runs with P = 0 only (the syscall gate normalizes before any syscall, and the boot path is mode 11), so the body is cold code

the driver boot gate (kernel/driver/driver_boot.asm): switches mode 10 over bank 6 (Q = 6) and calls a boot segment. Its code and continuation execute with bank 7 unmapped, so the gate is common-resident; its request and transition state is fixed-core data because the upcall shim reads the loader's request block with bank 7 mapped

cold_half_note: The production build compiles these objects into the cold areas (_WINDOW / _WINDOW_DATA at 6000h-DFFFh): the syscall dispatcher and its bodies (including the extended-memory family), the boot path, the process lifecycle, the VFS core and the resident-driver loader (the cold data base follows the linked cold code). tools/mapcheck.py fails the build when the linked cold code or data overruns the derived bases, and the fixed ledger reports the remaining fixed-core bytes.
